title: What If You Were Stuck in 1850 With Only Your Phone?
description:
September 1, 1850. You're on a New York wharf with tens of thousands of people waiting for Jenny Lind's ship, and in your pocket is your phone: 80% battery, no bars. Five attempts to make the most powerful machine on Earth matter, using real history only.

Chapters
0:00 Stuck in 1850
0:41 Who's on the ship
1:08 Attempt 1: Call someone
1:53 Attempt 2: Show it off
3:01 Attempt 3: Charge it
4:01 Attempt 4: Get it copied
5:02 Attempt 5: Save lives
6:08 What would actually have worked

Facts used: Jenny Lind's ship, the Atlantic, docked in New York on September 1, 1850, and the papers counted thirty or forty thousand people on the piers. About 12,000 miles of telegraph wire ran across the US in 1850. The first GPS satellite went up in 1978, New York's first power station opened in 1882, and the first transistor was built in 1947. Telegraph lines of the era favored the Grove cell, about 1.9 volts per jar. Joseph Henry ran the new Smithsonian from 1846. Cholera killed more than 5,000 New Yorkers in 1849 and about 2,500 more in 1854. In Vienna in 1847, Ignaz Semmelweis cut deaths on his ward from about 1 in 5 to about 1 in 50 with chlorinated-lime handwashing. In 1854 John Snow mapped London's cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump.

The charging plan is shown as a gamble the story never takes; whether a Grove battery would really charge a phone isn't claimed.
